title.rendered: Standing in the Gap: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: I sought for a man among them who would make a wall, and stand in the gap before Me on behalf of the land, that I should not destroy it; but I found no one. Intercession is authority in action.

content.rendered:
I sought for a man among them who would make a wall, and stand in the gap before Me on behalf of the land, that I should not destroy it; but I found no one. Intercession is authority in action. The believer who stands in the gap holds a wall no wave of judgement can break through.

The Gospel For Today | Friday, August 7, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“So I sought for a man among them who would make a wall, and stand in the gap before Me on behalf of the land, that I should not destroy it; but I found no one.”
Ezekiel 22:30 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Ezekiel 22 records one of the most sobering sentences in the entire Old Testament. God is looking over the land of Israel in a moment of national judgement. He is looking for one thing. An intercessor. A man who would make a wall. A man who would stand in the gap before Him on behalf of the land. The Lord says He sought for such a person, and He found no one. That absence is what precipitated the judgement that fell.

The Amplified Bible Classic Edition expands the picture: “And I sought a man among them who should build up the wall and stand in the gap before Me for the land, that I should not destroy it, but I found none” (Ezekiel 22:30 AMPC). The intercessor is not just a private prayer warrior. The intercessor is a wall-builder and a gap-stander. Their prayer keeps the wall of protection intact and prevents the flood of judgement from breaking through.

The New Testament raises the same call, this time as a positive assignment for the entire church. Paul writes to Timothy in 1 Timothy 2:1-4: “Therefore I exhort first of all that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men, for kings and all who are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and reverence. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, who desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth” (NKJV). Notice the priority. First of all. Before anything else the church does, it intercedes.

Intercession is one of the most powerful exercises of the believer’s authority. The intercessor stands, in Jesus’ name, in the gap between a person or nation and the outcome that would come if no one stood. The intercessor pushes back the darkness by prayer that agrees with heaven’s mercy over the situation. The intercessor does not act as their own authority. They act as one carrying the keys of the kingdom, using the name of Jesus, agreeing with the will of the Father, standing in the gap in the power of the Spirit.

For Gospelbuzz readers, this is the invitation. Do not be the gap that no one is standing in. Stand for your family. Stand for your city. Stand for your nation. Stand for the persecuted church. Stand for your unbelieving colleagues. Stand for the leaders whose decisions shape the lives of millions. Stand for the missionaries in dark places. The Lord is looking for those who will build walls and stand in gaps. Let Him find you today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have called me into the ministry of intercession. I am one who will stand in the gap. I refuse to leave the wall unbuilt. In the name of Jesus, I stand for my family today. I stand for the leaders of my nation. I stand for the persecuted church around the world. I stand for the unbelieving. I stand for the wounded. I agree with heaven’s mercy over every situation I bring before You. I use the keys of the kingdom Jesus has placed in my hands. Where You are looking for someone to stand in the gap, let You find me here. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am an intercessor. I stand in the gap in the name of Jesus. Where the Lord is looking for someone to build the wall, He finds me here.
